title: Transactional Min Stack
description:
Design a min-stack `TransactionalStack` that supports nested database-style transactions (`begin`, `rollback`, `commit`) alongside `O(1)` minimum queries.

Implement the `TransactionalStack` class:
- `TransactionalStack()` initializes an empty stack with no active transaction.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the stack.
- `int pop()` removes and returns the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `int getMin()` returns the minimum element currently in the stack.
- `void begin()` opens a new nested transaction block.
- `boolean rollback()` reverts all `push` and `pop` operations performed since the most recent open `begin()` and closes that transaction; returns `true` if a transaction was active, or `false` if no transaction is open.
- `boolean commit()` merges the most recent open transaction's changes into its enclosing transaction (or base state) and closes it; returns `true` if a transaction was active, or `false` otherwise.
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getMin are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Maintain a standard O(1) min-stack plus a stack of transaction undo logs, where each undo log records the inverse of every push or pop performed during that transaction.

Store each transaction's undo log as a singly linked list in reverse chronological order with (head, tail) pointers so push/pop prepend in O(1), commit splices into the parent list in O(1), and rollback replays from head in amortized O(1).

examples.explanation: Push 5 -> begin -> push 2 (min 2) -> rollback restores [5] (min 5); next begin -> push 1 -> commit makes [5, 1] permanent (min 1).
Calling rollback or commit when no transaction is open returns false.
Nested transactions allow committing an inner block into an outer block and later rolling back both together.
